summary.rationale: The 120-case set is designed for paper evaluation of PSQ-SCO against the prompt+RAG baseline. It uses 30 base groups from 3 channels x 2 variants x 5 roles. Each group is tested at three difficulty anchors, giving 90 cases. One balanced repetition is added per group, giving 30 more cases and a total of 120. The repetition is not random duplication: it rotates through the six non-anchor stages and all five age groups so the sample can test stability, age suitability, and non-anchor stage behavior without expanding to the full 1,350-slot scenario space.
summary.base_group_formula: 3 channels x 2 variants x 5 roles = 30 base groups
summary.difficulty_formula: 30 base groups x 3 difficulty anchors = 90 cases
summary.balanced_repetition_formula: 30 base groups x 1 balanced repetition = 30 cases

cases.rationale: Low difficulty anchor: explicit cues, foundational recognition, high scaffolding.
Medium difficulty anchor: multiple cues, applied comparison, moderate ambiguity.
High difficulty anchor: subtle cues, strategic reflection, low explicit scaffolding.
Balanced repetition: one additional matched case per base group to test stability, age rotation, and non-anchor stage behavior.
